record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is it possible to avoid an arbitrary pattern p by an inﬁ- nite sequence of palindromes over each alphabet on which p is avoidable?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to avoid an arbitrary pattern p by an inﬁ- nite sequence of palindromes over each alphabet on which p is avoidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let A* denote the set of finite words over A. Let E be a separate alphabet of "pattern variables." A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E*. A word w ∈ A* is said to contain the pattern p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h: E* → A* (i.e. h(e) is nonempty for every variable e ∈ E) such that h(p) is a factor (contiguous subword) of w; otherwise w avoids p. The pattern p is said to be avoidable on A if there exists an infinite word over A all of whose finite factors avoid p. A finite word u ∈ A* is a palindrome if u equals its reversal.

Question: For every pattern p ∈ E* and every finite alphabet A on which p is avoidable, does there exist an infinite word w over A that avoids p and that can be written as an infinite concatenation w = u₁u₂u₃··· where each uᵢ is a (nonempty) palindrome over A?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface related work on palindrome-pattern avoidability (e.g., Ochem–Rosenfeld, "Avoidability of Palindrome Patterns," Electron. J. Combin. 2021), but none directly answer whether every avoidable pattern can be avoided by an infinite concatenation of palindromes on every alphabet on which it is avoidable. The problem appears in lists of WORDS-conference open problems and no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of Palindrome Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes formulas avoided by α-free words; works toward conjecture that every avoidable palindrome pattern is 4-avoidable.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work on palindrome patterns, but does not address concatenations of palindromes avoiding an arbitrary avoidable pattern.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding or Limiting Regularities in Words
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on pattern avoidance and palindromic factor restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys the area without resolving the stated WORDS open problem.
